items.title: Ed Garland Interview, 1971-04-20
items.q: I had a band. I had a band. Manuel Perez on trumpet.

ctx.x: Was he hotter than Manuel Perez?

I'm going to tell you that there you are, there's two good men, two good men you call in there, Manuel and Kimball. Both. I don't know, I don't know, there wasn't a mood. There wasn't too hot on the jazz, you know. They played, there was good trumpet players.
Good musician, good trumpet players. Oh my goodness.

items.title: 68090_Ed Garland oral history interview
items.q: And I played out there with Manuel. He had an awful band out there. Manuel got me to play with him.

ctx.x: I'd take Manuel Perez. Dusen. Frankie Dawson.

items.title: Ed Garland Interview, 1957-04-16
items.q: I used to have Manuel, Teo, Frankie Enya, see, and, uh, Eddie Atkins on some bones.

ctx.x: No. Mabel Elaine and her jazz band. She's a white girl. She used to clunk band. You know how Boa Jingles used to dance with wooden shoes on. She had the same thing. She used to be in a bale of cotton. She was blackface. When you get on the stage, that bale of cotton was out there. They couldn't go out. We'd be all lying around in this cotton, see, with a couple of holes on, satin cover holes, different colors, and bandana, hangers, and hats. So I had, when we started playing, this fave of cotton opened up. And…
